elements.element: Covered indemnitees include Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: The Ono Indemnitees expressly include Ono and its Affiliates, as well as additional related persons.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies and holds harmless the covered Customer parties from liabilities arising from covered third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Array must “indemnify and hold harmless” the Ono Indemnitees from “any and all Liabilities from any Third Party Claims.”

elements.element: Vendor has an affirmative duty to defend all covered third-party claims against Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: No affirmative Array defense duty is included. For Infringement Actions, the Subject Party instead controls the defense at its own expense, meaning Ono must defend itself when it is the Subject Party.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers third-party claims alleging that the services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Added subsection (e) covers allegations that the Development, Manufacture, registration, use, or Commercialization of a Product in the Ono Territory infringes or misappropriates third-party intellectual property rights.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers third-party claims arising from Vendor's breach of law.
elements.evidence: The clause does not expressly cover Array's breach of law. Subsection (d) covers breaches of Article 15 representations, warranties, or covenants, but the contents of Article 15 do not demonstrate a coextensive breach-of-law indemnity.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers third-party claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No data-breach indemnity trigger appears.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers third-party claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: The clause contains only an exclusion for claims resulting from an Ono Indemnitee's gross negligence or willful misconduct; it does not create indemnity for Array's gross negligence or willful misconduct.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires Customer to give Vendor prompt notice of every covered indemnity claim.
elements.evidence: Prompt written notice is required only for defined Infringement Actions and is not established as the procedure for all claims covered by Section 16.2.

elements.element: Vendor controls the defense and settlement of covered indemnity claims, subject to customary Customer protections.
elements.evidence: The Subject Party, rather than Array as indemnitor, has sole control of an Infringement Action and bears its own expense. No general Vendor settlement-control procedure is provided.

elements.element: Customer must provide reasonable cooperation in the defense of covered claims, ordinarily at Vendor's expense.
elements.evidence: The obligation to discuss strategy and keep the other party informed does not impose a customary cooperation duty, and participation is expressly at the other party's own expense.

elements.element: Any indemnity given by Customer is limited to third-party claims arising from Customer-provided content or Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause imposes no Ono-to-Array indemnity, so the condition is demonstrably absent and no broader Customer indemnity is created here.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party claims alleging intellectual property infringement or misappropriation by the contractual products or deliverables.
elements.evidence: Subsection (e) provides an Array indemnity for third-party allegations that specified Product activities in the Ono Territory infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity excludes infringement caused by Customer's modifications.
elements.evidence: There is no exclusion for modifications made by Ono or another Customer-side party.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity excludes infringement caused by combinations with items not supplied or authorized by Vendor.
elements.evidence: There is no combination exclusion.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity excludes infringement resulting from compliance with Customer-provided specifications.
elements.evidence: There is no Customer-specifications exclusion.

elements.element: Vendor must procure the necessary rights as an infringement remedy.
elements.evidence: No obligation to procure continued usage or commercialization rights appears.

elements.element: Vendor must modify the affected product or deliverable to make it non-infringing as an infringement remedy.
elements.evidence: No non-infringing modification remedy appears.

elements.element: Vendor must replace the affected product or deliverable with a non-infringing alternative as an infringement remedy.
elements.evidence: No replacement remedy appears.

elements.element: Vendor must provide a refund if the other infringement remedies are unavailable or unsuccessful.
elements.evidence: No refund remedy or remedy sequence appears.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity liability is subject to a super-cap equal to three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3× annual-fees cap or other express indemnity super-cap appears in the rendered language.

result.reason: The redline adds a usable Vendor IP indemnity, but it does not provide a Vendor defense duty, the other preferred indemnity triggers, or a standard indemnification procedure. It also omits every specified fallback exclusion, remedy, and the 3× super-cap. The existing provision allowing the Subject Party to control an infringement defense at its own expense creates tension with Array's new obligation to indemnify Ono for the same claims, and moving subsection (a) ahead of the Section 16.2 heading produces defective structure. Because neither complete position is reached, the redline is not minimal for purposes of the rule.
